mainTopic: How responsible a lender is for collateral, renting out a poor person's collateral, and the case of a watchman who breaks a barrel while carrying it
overview: The amud opens by finishing the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about a lender who loses collateral. It pins their argument to a lender who wants to use the collateral, and asks whether his lending still counts as a מצוה. Next the גמרא brings אבא שאול's rule that a lender may rent out a poor person's collateral to pay down the debt. שמואל rules like אבא שאול, but only for sturdy tools that earn high rent and wear down little. A new משנה then teaches that a watchman who broke a barrel while carrying it swears and goes free. רבי אליעזר agrees with this ruling but says he is puzzled by it. A ברייתא shows that this view belongs to רבי מאיר, while רבי יהודה says a paid watchman must pay. The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can say this, since elsewhere he treats one who stumbles as careless. רבי אלעזר answers that the two sources hold different traditions of רבי מאיר's view. Finally the גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's puzzle. A paid watchman pays even without carelessness, and an unpaid one can only honestly swear if the barrel broke on a slope.

steps.title: The argument is about a lender who wants to use the collateral
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא disagree in the case of a lender who wants to use the collateral. One side says he is still doing a מצוה and so is a שומר שכר. The other says he is lending for his own benefit and so is only a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about a lender who needs the collateral. One Sage holds that he is doing a מצוה by lending, so he is a paid watchman. The other Sage holds that he is not doing a מצוה, since he means it for his own benefit, so he is an unpaid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its explanation of what רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא are really arguing about when a lender loses the collateral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a lender who wants to use the collateral and take its value off the loan. One view holds that his lending still counts as a מצוה, and the benefit of doing that מצוה makes him like a paid watchman (שומר שכר), so he must pay for loss. The other view holds that lending for his own gain is not a מצוה, so he is just an unpaid watchman (שומר חנם) and can swear and go free.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral, an item given to secure a loan
A paid watchman, who must pay if the item is lost or stolen
An unpaid watchman, who only pays for carelessness and can swear to go free

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a lender counts as a שומר שכר or a שומר חנם for collateral depends on whether his lending is a מצוה or done for his own benefit.

phrases.english: They disagree about a lender who needs the collateral.
phrases.notes: "Needs the collateral" means he wants to use it and take what it is worth off the loan.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵיד שֶׁהִלְוָהוּ,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: he is doing a מצוה by lending to him,
and so he is a paid watchman.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָאו מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵיד,
phrases.english: And one Sage holds: he is not doing a מצוה,
since he intends it for his own benefit,
and so he is an unpaid watchman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion about what רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא disagree on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pins the מחלוקת to a specific case: a lender who wants to use the collateral
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think they argue about collateral in every loan
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only where the lender wants to use the collateral, because the question is whether that lending is still a מצוה

steps.title: אבא שאול: you may rent out a poor person's collateral
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אבא שאול from the משנה. He allows a lender to rent out a poor person's collateral so the rent slowly pays down the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: A person may rent out a poor person's collateral, so that the debt keeps getting smaller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה, אבא שאול's rule, to set up a ruling about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a lender should not use the borrower's collateral for his own gain. אבא שאול allows renting it out when the borrower is poor, because the rent money goes toward the loan and the poor man's debt shrinks.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps going down little by little

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
A person is permitted to rent out
the collateral of a poor person
so that it keeps going down.
phrases.notes: What goes down is the loan: each rent payment is taken off what the poor man owes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next statement in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender may rent out a poor borrower's collateral and take the rent off the debt.

steps.title: שמואל rules like אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר אמי reports in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a practical ruling: we follow אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול's view is not just a side opinion in the משנה. שמואל makes it the practical הלכה, so a lender really may rent out a poor person's collateral.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Ami said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Abba Shaul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the statement quoted in step 2.

steps.title: Only for tools that earn a lot and wear down little
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits אבא שאול's rule to tools like a hoe, a chisel, and an ax. Their rent is high and renting them hardly damages them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even אבא שאול only said this about a hoe, a chisel, and an ax, because they earn a lot of rent and wear down only a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling is narrowed: renting out a poor person's collateral is allowed only for certain sturdy tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting is good for the poor man only if the rent he gains is worth more than the damage to his item. Sturdy work tools bring in high rent and barely wear out, so renting clearly helps him. Items that wear out fast would hurt him, so the rule does not cover them.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows אבא שאול, but only for collateral whose rent is high and whose wear is small, such as a hoe, a chisel, or an ax.

phrases.english: And even Abba Shaul said it only
about a hoe, a chisel, and an ax,
since their rental pay is large
and their wear is small.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף אַבָּא שָׁאוּל לָא אָמַר אֶלָּא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול's permission applies only to items with high rent and little wear.

steps.title: New משנה: a watchman who breaks a barrel while carrying it
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that anyone who broke a barrel while moving it, whether a שומר חנם or a שומר שכר, swears that he was not careless and goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who was moving a barrel from place to place and broke it, whether he is an unpaid watchman or a paid watchman, swears.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case: a watchman broke a barrel while carrying it, and the ruling is that he swears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a שומר שכר must pay even for theft or loss, more than a שומר חנם does. This משנה treats both the same here: each one swears that he was not careless and pays nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: One who moves or carries something across
A barrel or jug, usually for wine or oil
He swears an oath and goes free

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a שומר שכר always pays. In this barrel case the משנה says even he can swear and go free.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who moves a barrel from place to place and breaks it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר – יִשָּׁבַע.
phrases.english: whether an unpaid watchman or a paid watchman, swears.
phrases.notes: He swears that he was not careless, and then he does not have to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both a שומר חנם and a שומר שכר who broke a barrel while moving it swear and go free.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר agrees but wonders how this can be
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר repeats that both watchmen swear, but says he does not understand how both of them can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Both this one and that one swear, and I wonder whether both this one and that one can really swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר passes on the same ruling but says he is puzzled by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not give a different ruling. He reports what he received, that both swear, but he finds it hard: why should a שומר שכר, who normally pays more, get to swear like a שומר חנם? The גמרא will explain his difficulty later.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both kinds of watchman

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not arguing about the ruling. He agrees that both swear and only says he does not understand why.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זֶה וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: This one and that one swear,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יְכוֹלִין זֶה וָזֶה לִישָּׁבַע.
phrases.english: and I wonder whether this one and that one can swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יְכוֹלִין זֶה וָזֶה לִישָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי אליעזר's view to the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both swear, but רבי אליעזר questions how this works.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the משנה's first opinion is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same case. It tells us that the view that both watchmen swear belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: Someone who was moving a barrel for his friend from place to place and broke it, whether an unpaid watchman or a paid watchman, swears. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that repeats the משנה's case and names who holds the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave its first ruling without a name. The ברייתא shows it is רבי מאיר. It also prepares us for another opinion, in the next step, that the משנה did not mention.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּעֲבִיר חָבִית לַחֲבֵירוֹ מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם וּשְׁבָרָהּ,
phrases.english: One who moves a barrel for his friend from place to place and breaks it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר – יִשָּׁבַע,
phrases.english: whether an unpaid watchman or a paid watchman, swears;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that names the author of the משנה's first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, both watchmen swear and go free.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the paid watchman pays
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. A שומר חנם swears, but a paid watchman must pay for the broken barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: An unpaid watchman swears, but one who takes pay must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion, רבי יהודה, who treats the paid watchman more strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה follows the usual rule that a שומר שכר carries more responsibility than a שומר חנם. So in the barrel case, the unpaid watchman swears and goes free, while the paid one has to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes pay, which is a שומר שכר

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
An unpaid watchman swears,
one who takes pay must pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם יִשָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about the paid watchman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר חנם swears, but a שומר שכר pays.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's puzzle, repeated in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's words from the משנה: both swear, but he wonders how both can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Both this one and that one swear, and I wonder whether both this one and that one can really swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats רבי אליעזר's statement, now beside the opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's ruling matches רבי מאיר's, but he is puzzled by it. This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion in steps 14 and 15 of what exactly he finds hard, which covers both the paid and the unpaid watchman.
steps.whatToRemember: In the barrel case רבי מאיר says both watchmen swear, רבי יהודה says the paid watchman pays, and רבי אליעזר rules that both swear but is puzzled by it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זֶה וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: This one and that one swear,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יְכוֹלִין זֶה וָזֶה לִישָּׁבַע.
phrases.english: and I wonder whether this one and that one can swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר זֶה וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by adding רבי אליעזר's view beside רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both swear, though רבי אליעזר questions how.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really think stumbling is not carelessness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's view that both watchmen swear. In another ברייתא he holds that one who stumbles is careless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבי מאיר thinks a person who stumbles is not careless? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone's pitcher broke and he did not clear it away, or his camel fell and he did not stand it up, רבי מאיר makes him pay for the damage. The חכמים say a human court cannot make him pay, but he is liable in the eyes of Heaven. And we know their argument is about whether one who stumbles is careless!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי מאיר's ruling that both watchmen may swear. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר seems to hold the opposite idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a watchman may swear and go free after breaking the barrel, then breaking it by stumbling is not carelessness. But in the pitcher-and-camel ברייתא, רבי מאיר makes the person pay. We know that argument is about whether a נתקל is a פושע. So רבי מאיר seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (opens a challenge to an implied idea)

keyTerms.term: פָּטוּר מִדִּינֵי אָדָם וְחַיָּיב בְּדִינֵי שָׁמַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: a human court cannot make him pay, but he owes it in the eyes of Heaven
we hold; it is established for us

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Meir holds
phrases.notes: He means: since רבי מאיר lets the watchman swear that he was not careless when the barrel broke.

phrases.english: that one who stumbles is not careless?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If his pitcher broke and he did not remove it,
or his camel fell and he did not stand it up,
Rabbi Meir makes him liable for the damage they cause,
and the Sages say:
he is exempt under the laws of human courts
but liable under the laws of Heaven.
And we hold
that they disagree about whether one who stumbles is careless!
phrases.notes: So רבי מאיר, who makes him pay, must hold that stumbling is carelessness.

steps.triggerLanguage: למימרא דסבר רבי מאיר נתקל לאו פושע הוא? והתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in step 7, that רבי מאיר holds both watchmen swear.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that both watchmen swear after the barrel breaks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Letting the watchman swear means stumbling is not carelessness. Elsewhere רבי מאיר makes a stumbler pay, so for him stumbling is carelessness. That is a contradiction.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the two ברייתות hold different traditions of רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the two ברייתות come from different תנאים with different traditions about רבי מאיר. The one who taught this ברייתא (both watchmen swear) did not teach that one (the pitcher and the camel).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Break it apart. Whoever taught this did not teach that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction by saying the barrel teaching and the pitcher-and-camel ברייתא come from two different traditions about what רבי מאיר held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to make רבי מאיר agree with himself. One תנא reported that for רבי מאיר stumbling is not carelessness, so both watchmen swear. Another תנא reported that for רבי מאיר stumbling is carelessness (the pitcher and camel). The next steps explain how רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר fit into the barrel ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: break it, meaning split the teaching apart

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: whoever taught this did not teach that

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר (אלעזר) here is a later אמורא who explains the ברייתא. רבי אליעזר (אליעזר) is the תנא quoted inside the ברייתא. The names look almost the same, but they are two different people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Break it,
phrases.notes: He means: these two sources don't come from the same teacher. Each one holds a different tradition of רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: whoever taught this did not teach that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר: תברה, מי ששנה זו לא שנה זו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different traditions of רבי מאיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות report the same view of רבי מאיר, so he seems to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different תנאים held different traditions of רבי מאיר's view, so the contradiction falls away.

steps.title: רבי יהודה gives each watchman his own law
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי אלעזר's reading, רבי יהודה teaches that the unpaid watchman swears and the paid watchman pays. Each one follows his normal law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה came to say: an unpaid watchman swears, and a paid watchman pays. This one follows his law, and that one follows his law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי אלעזר's answer by explaining what רבי יהודה's part of the ברייתא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה applies the normal rules of watchmen to the broken barrel. A שומר חנם is free if he was not careless, so he swears. A שומר שכר has stricter responsibility, so he pays. On the paid watchman, this disagrees with the tradition that both swear.

keyTerms.meaning: a paid watchman (literally, one who takes pay)
this one according to his own law

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda came to say:
an unpaid watchman swears,
a paid watchman pays.
This one according to his law,
and that one according to his law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's answer by explaining רבי יהודה's piece of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining one piece of the split ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה simply applies each watchman's normal rules.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר confirms the tradition but wonders about it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר confirms that there is a tradition following רבי מאיר, but he questions whether both watchmen can really swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר came to say: Yes, there is a tradition that follows רבי מאיר. But I wonder whether both this one and that one can swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי אלעזר's split. רבי אליעזר's line confirms that the both-swear view was received as a tradition, even though he is puzzled by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the both-swear view was handed down as a received teaching, separate from רבי מאיר's other rulings. רבי אליעזר accepts that it was taught but finds it hard to understand. The next steps explain exactly what puzzles him.

keyTerms.meaning: a received tradition (a teaching handed down from teachers)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer came to say:
Yes, there is a tradition following Rabbi Meir.
But I wonder
whether this one and that one can swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואתא רבי אליעזר למימר: אין, גמרא כרבי מאיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אלעזר's reading by explaining רבי אליעזר's line in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the last piece of the split ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The both-swear view is a received tradition, which רבי אליעזר accepts but finds puzzling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the sugya, which explains what makes רבי אליעזר wonder.

steps.title: Why should a paid watchman be allowed to swear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains part of רבי אליעזר's wonder. A paid watchman has to pay even when he was not careless, so swearing should not help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that an unpaid watchman swears that he was not careless with the barrel. But why does a paid watchman swear? Even if he was not careless, he still has to pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why רבי אליעזר is puzzled. It starts with the paid watchman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם is free as long as he was not careless, so his oath makes sense. A שומר שכר owes more than that, so even if he was not careless he still has to pay. An oath that he was not careless should not free him.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense for... (this part is fine)

phrases.english: It makes sense for an unpaid watchman:
he swears that he was not careless with it.
But a paid watchman, why does he swear?
Even when he was not careless,
he still has to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא שומר חנם משתבע דלא פשע בה: אלא שומר שכר אמאי משתבע?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first reason for רבי אליעזר's wonder in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the paid watchman may swear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A paid watchman pays even without carelessness, so an oath that he was not careless cannot free him.

steps.title: Even the unpaid watchman can only swear if he was on a slope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that even the unpaid watchman's oath only makes sense if the barrel broke on a slope. Otherwise, breaking it shows he was careless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the unpaid watchman: that works if it happened on a slope. But if it was not on a slope, how can he swear that he was not careless with it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי אליעזר's wonder by questioning the unpaid watchman too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a slope, the barrel could break even with no carelessness, so the unpaid watchman can honestly swear. On flat ground, breaking it points to carelessness, so he cannot honestly swear. That is why רבי אליעזר wonders that both watchmen can swear.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's wonder has two parts. A paid watchman pays even without carelessness, so his oath shouldn't help. And an unpaid watchman can only honestly swear if the barrel broke on a slope.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואפילו שומר חנם נמי, התינח במקום מדרון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question from the paid watchman (step 14) to the unpaid watchman.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the unpaid watchman may swear in every case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Away from a slope, breaking the barrel points to carelessness, so he cannot honestly swear that he was not careless.
